speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with episodes of painful urination and a history of a painful, swollen left ankle. Let's start by asking: how many years has it been since your left ankle episode resolved?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The timeline of your ankle swelling (resolving about a week ago) followed by new knee symptoms and urinary pain strongly suggests a specific type of infection. Given your sexual history and inconsistent condom use, is there any chance you have been exposed to chlamydia or gonorrhea, or do you notice any other joint swelling?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (NAAT) for Chlamydia/Gonorrhea.
